en: He had just been released.
ko: 그는 방금 풀려났다.

raw: Charles Darnay--just released--congratulating him on his escape from death.
en: They were congratulating him on his narrow escape from death.
ko: 그들은 그가 가까스로 죽음을 모면한 것을 축하하고 있었다.

raw: It would have been difficult by a far brighter light, to recognise in Doctor Manette, intellectual of face and upright of bearing, the shoemaker of the garret in Paris.
en: Even in much brighter light, it would have been hard to recognize the old shoemaker from the Paris attic in the intellectual-looking and upright Doctor Manette.
ko: 훨씬 더 밝은 빛 속에서도, 지적으로 보이고 꼿꼿한 마네트 박사에게서 파리 다락방의 늙은 구두장이를 알아보기는 어려웠을 것이다.

raw: Yet, no one could have looked at him twice, without looking again: even though the opportunity of observation had not extended to the mournful cadence of his low grave voice, and to the abstraction that overclouded him fitfully, without any apparent reason.
en: Yet no one could look at him once without looking again. He still spoke in a sad, grave voice and would occasionally fall into a quiet, distracted state for no apparent reason.
ko: 하지만 누구도 그를 한 번 보고 다시 보지 않을 수 없었다. 그는 여전히 슬프고 진지한 목소리로 말했고, 이따금 뚜렷한 이유 없이 조용하고 멍한 상태에 빠지곤 했다.

raw: While one external cause, and that a reference to his long lingering agony, would always--as on the trial--evoke this condition from the depths of his soul, it was also in its nature to arise of itself, and to draw a gloom over him, as incomprehensible to those unacquainted with his story as if they had seen the shadow of the actual Bastille thrown upon him by a summer sun, when the substance was three hundred miles away.
en: While referencing his long years of suffering in prison would always trigger this state, as it had during the trial, it could also happen on its own, casting a shadow over him. To anyone who did not know his story, it was deeply puzzling. It was as if the shadow of the Bastille prison had fallen across him right there in the bright summer sun. The prison itself was hundreds of miles away, but the shadow was very real.
ko: 재판 때처럼 감옥에서의 오랜 고통을 언급하는 것은 항상 이런 상태를 유발했지만, 그 자체로도 일어날 수 있었고 그에게 그림자를 드리웠다. 그의 이야기를 모르는 사람에게 그것은 깊이 당혹스러운 일이었다. 마치 바스티유 감옥의 그림자가 바로 그곳, 밝은 여름 햇살 속에 있는 그에게 드리워진 것 같았다. 감옥 자체는 수백 마일 떨어져 있었지만, 그림자는 매우 현실적이었다.

raw: Only his daughter had the power of charming this black brooding from his mind.
en: Only his daughter had the power to chase away these dark moods.
ko: 오직 그의 딸만이 이 어두운 기분을 쫓아낼 힘이 있었다.

raw: She was the golden thread that united him to a Past beyond his misery, and to a Present beyond his misery: and the sound of her voice, the light of her face, the touch of her hand, had a strong beneficial influence with him almost always.
en: She was the golden thread that connected him to a past and a present beyond his years of misery. The sound of her voice, the look on her face, and the touch of her hand almost always had a powerful, healing effect on him.
ko: 그녀는 그의 불행했던 세월 너머의 과거와 현재를 연결해 주는 황금 실이었다. 그녀의 목소리, 그녀의 얼굴 표정, 그리고 그녀의 손길은 거의 항상 그에게 강력하고 치유적인 효과를 주었다.

raw: Not absolutely always, for she could recall some occasions on which her power had failed; but they were few and slight, and she believed them over.
en: It was not absolutely always, as there were a few times when her influence had failed, but those moments were rare, and she believed they were behind them.
ko: 그녀의 영향력이 통하지 않았던 때가 몇 번 있었기 때문에 절대적으로 항상 그런 것은 아니었지만, 그런 순간은 드물었고, 그녀는 그것들이 이미 지나갔다고 믿었다.

raw: Stryver, a man of little more than thirty, but looking twenty years older than he was, stout, loud, red, bluff, and free from any drawback of delicacy, had a pushing way of shouldering himself (morally and physically) into companies and conversations, that argued well for his shouldering his way up in life.
en: He was heavily built and loud. His face was red. He was blunt, and he completely lacked politeness or tact. He had a pushy habit of forcing his way into groups and conversations, which suggested he would have no trouble pushing his way up in the world.
ko: 그는 체격이 크고 목소리가 컸다. 그의 얼굴은 붉었다. 그는 퉁명스러웠고, 예의나 눈치가 전혀 없었다. 그는 무리나 대화에 억지로 끼어드는 뻔뻔한 버릇이 있었는데, 이는 그가 세상에서 출세하는 데 아무런 문제가 없을 것임을 암시했다.

ko: 다네이, 그리고 제 최선은 다른 누구의 것 못지않게 훌륭하다고 믿습니다."

en: Darnay, and for Miss Lucie. Miss Lucie, don't you agree I should speak for us all?" He asked her directly, with a glance at her father.

raw: His face had become frozen, as it were, in a very curious look at Darnay: an intent look, deepening into a frown of dislike and distrust, not even unmixed with fear.
en: Doctor Manette's face had frozen into a strange look as he stared at Darnay. It was an intense look that deepened into a frown of dislike and distrust, mixed with a hint of fear.
ko: 다네이를 응시하는 마네트 박사의 얼굴은 이상한 표정으로 굳어 있었다. 그것은 약간의 두려움이 섞인 강렬한 시선이었고, 싫어함과 불신의 찡그림으로 깊어졌다.

raw: With this strange expression on him his thoughts had wandered away.
en: With this strange expression on his face, his mind seemed to wander far away.
ko: 이런 이상한 표정을 얼굴에 띠고, 그의 마음은 아주 멀리 방황하는 듯했다.

raw: “My father,” said Lucie, softly laying her hand on his.
en: "Father," Lucie said softly, laying her hand on his arm.
ko: "아버지," 루시가 그의 팔에 손을 얹으며 부드럽게 말했다.

raw: He slowly shook the shadow off, and turned to her.
en: He slowly shook off the dark mood and turned to her.
ko: 그는 천천히 어두운 기분을 떨쳐내고 그녀에게 몸을 돌렸다.

raw: “Shall we go home, my father?”
en: "Shall we go home, father?"
ko: "우리 집에 갈까요, 아버지?"

en: Taking a deep breath, he answered, "Yes."
ko: 깊은숨을 쉬고, 그는 대답했다. "그래."

raw: The friends of the acquitted prisoner had dispersed, under the impression--which he himself had originated--that he would not be released that night.
en: The friends of the acquitted prisoner had already left, believing Darnay would not be released until the next morning.
ko: 무죄 판결을 받은 죄수의 친구들은 다네이가 다음날 아침까지 풀려나지 않을 것이라 믿고 이미 떠난 상태였다.

raw: The lights were nearly all extinguished in the passages, the iron gates were being closed with a jar and a rattle, and the dismal place was deserted until to-morrow morning’s interest of gallows, pillory, whipping-post, and branding-iron, should repeople it.
en: Most of the lights in the hallways were turned off. The iron gates were closing with a loud rattle. The gloomy courthouse was deserted. It would remain empty until the next day's crowd arrived for more hangings, whippings, and brandings.
ko: 복도의 조명은 대부분 꺼져 있었다. 철문들이 요란한 소리를 내며 닫히고 있었다. 어두침침한 법정은 인적이 끊겼다. 다음 날 더 많은 교수형, 채찍질, 낙형을 보기 위해 군중이 도착할 때까지 그곳은 텅 비어 있을 것이다.

ko: 다네이 사이를 걸으며, 루시 마네트는 신선한 공기 속으로 걸어 나왔다.

en: A carriage was called, and the father and daughter drove away.

raw: Another person, who had not joined the group, or interchanged a word with any one of them, but who had been leaning against the wall where its shadow was darkest, had silently strolled out after the rest, and had looked on until the coach drove away.
en: Another person, who had not joined the group or spoken to anyone, had been leaning against the wall in the darkest shadow. He quietly walked out after them and watched until the carriage drove off.
ko: 그 무리에 끼지도 않고 누구에게도 말을 걸지 않았던 다른 한 사람이 가장 짙은 그림자 속 벽에 기대어 있었다. 그는 조용히 그들의 뒤를 따라나와 마차가 떠날 때까지 지켜보았다.

en: He had taken off his lawyer's robes and looked no better for it.
ko: 그는 법복을 벗었지만, 그로 인해 결코 더 나아 보이지는 않았다.

en: Carton spoke first. "If you knew the conflict that goes on in a businessman's head, you would be amused, Mr. Darnay," he said.
ko: 카턴이 먼저 말했다. "사업가의 머릿속에서 일어나는 갈등을 아신다면 재미있으실 겁니다, 미스터 다네이," 그가 말했다.

raw: Darnay.”

ko: 회사를 섬기는 우리 사업가들은 우리 자신의 주인이 아닙니다.

ko: 우리는 우리 자신보다 은행의 평판을 먼저 생각해야 합니다."

en: "_I_ know, _I_ know," Carton said carelessly.
ko: "압니다, 알아요," 카턴이 무심하게 말했다.

raw: Here, they were shown into a little room, where Charles Darnay was soon recruiting his strength with a good plain dinner and good wine: while Carton sat opposite to him at the same table, with his separate bottle of port before him, and his fully half-insolent manner upon him.
en: They were shown into a small room, where Darnay began to regain his strength with a plain dinner and good wine. Carton sat opposite him at the table with his own bottle of port, maintaining his rude, half-insolent manner.
ko: 그들은 작은 방으로 안내되었고, 다네이는 소박한 저녁 식사와 좋은 와인으로 기운을 차리기 시작했다. 카턴은 테이블 맞은편에 자신만의 포트와인 한 병을 놓고 앉아 그의 무례하고 반쯤 건방진 태도를 유지했다.

raw: “Do you feel, yet, that you belong to this terrestrial scheme again, Mr.

ko: 카턴은 "전혀 그렇지 않죠."라고 말하며 동의했다. 다네이가 계산을 했다. "당신이 전부 지불하는 겁니까?" 카턴이 물었다.

ko: 다네이 씨, 당신은 내가 취했다고 생각합니까?"

raw: “I think you have been drinking, Mr.
en: "I think you have been drinking, Mr.
ko: "당신이 술을 마셨다고 생각합니다,

raw: Carton.”
en: Carton."
ko: 카턴 씨."

raw: “Think?
en: "Think?
ko: "생각해?

raw: I care for no man on earth, and no man on earth cares for me.”
en: I care for no one on earth, and no one on earth cares for me."
ko: 나는 세상 그 누구에게도 관심이 없고, 세상 그 누구도 나에게 관심이 없지."

raw: “Much to be regretted.
en: "That is very regrettable.
ko: "그건 참 유감이군요.

raw: You might have used your talents better.”
en: You could have used your talents better."
ko: 당신은 당신의 재능을 더 잘 사용할 수도 있었을 텐데요."

raw: “May be so, Mr.
en: "Maybe so, Mr.
ko: "그럴지도 모르죠,

raw: Don’t let your sober face elate you, however; you don’t know what it may come to.
en: But don't let your sober face make you feel too proud; you don't know what you might become.
ko: 하지만 당신의 멀쩡한 얼굴 때문에 너무 교만해하지는 마쇼. 당신이 어떻게 될지 당신도 모르는 일이니.

raw: Good night!”
en: Good night!"
ko: 안녕히!"

raw: When he was left alone, this strange being took up a candle, went to a glass that hung against the wall, and surveyed himself minutely in it.
en: Left alone, Carton took a candle, went to a mirror on the wall, and studied his face closely.
ko: 홀로 남은 카턴은 촛불을 들고 벽에 있는 거울로 가서 자신의 얼굴을 자세히 살펴보았다.

raw: “Do you particularly like the man?” he muttered, at his own image; “why should you particularly like a man who resembles you?
en: "Do you like this man?" he muttered to his own reflection.
ko: "너는 이 사람을 좋아하느냐?" 그는 거울에 비친 자신에게 중얼거렸다.

raw: There is nothing in you to like; you know that.
en: "Why should you like a man who looks like you?
ko: "왜 너는 너처럼 생긴 사람을 좋아해야 하지?

raw: Ah, confound you!
en: There is nothing in you to like, and you know it.
ko: 너한테는 좋아하는 구석이 아무것도 없고, 네가 그걸 알고 있잖아.

raw: What a change you have made in yourself!
en: Look at how much you've changed yourself!
ko: 네가 얼마나 많이 변했는지 좀 봐라!

raw: A good reason for taking to a man, that he shows you what you have fallen away from, and what you might have been!
en: It's a great reason to like a man, when he shows you exactly what you've thrown away and the person you could have become!
ko: 네가 버린 것과 네가 될 수도 있었을 사람을 정확히 보여주니, 누군가를 좋아하기에 참 훌륭한 이유구나!

raw: Change places with him, and would you have been looked at by those blue eyes as he was, and commiserated by that agitated face as he was?
en: It's a fine reason to like a man because he shows you what you used to be and what you could have been!
ko: 누군가를 좋아하기에 참 좋은 이유지, 왜냐하면 그가 예전의 너와 네가 될 수 있었던 모습을 보여주니까!

raw: Come on, and have it out in plain words!
en: If you changed places with him, would those blue eyes look at you with such pity and love?
ko: 만약 네가 그와 자리를 바꾼다면, 그 푸른 눈이 그렇게 큰 연민과 사랑으로 너를 바라볼까?

raw: You hate the fellow.”
en: Let's be honest about it: you hate him."
ko: 솔직해지자, 넌 그를 미워하고 있어.

raw: He resorted to his pint of wine for consolation, drank it all in a few minutes, and fell asleep on his arms, with his hair straggling over the table, and a long winding-sheet in the candle dripping down upon him.
en: He drank the rest of his wine in a few minutes to comfort himself. Then he fell asleep with his head on his arms. His hair was messy on the table. The candle melted down quietly beside him.
ko: 그는 스스로를 달래기 위해 남은 포도주를 단 몇 분 만에 다 마셔버렸다. 그러고는 팔에 머리를 기댄 채 잠이 들었다. 그의 머리카락은 탁자 위에 헝클어져 있었다. 양초는 그의 곁에서 조용히 녹아내렸다.
